questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I've only been doing clinical rotation, which is why the language was crucial. I wanted to speak with the patients in their native language. I already speak german, which is why I chose Germany.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
Berlin is amazing and it's very easy to get to know people here. They also organize events with Erasmus students from all over Europe and I got an Erasmus-Buddy, a german medical student, who became my friend right from the beginning. 
On the other hand as a student you're not allowed to do as much in the hospital in Germany as you are in Denmark, so I didn't learn as much as I could have in Denmark. So I didn't learn as much accademically as I hoped I would. It was very nice and interesting to see how they do stuff in Germany though. 
Lastly I think it's a pitty that there is so much bureaucracy involved in a Erasmus program.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Easy. Everyone was very helpful and it was easy to get in touch with the coordinator in Berlin.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer:
I didn't receive assistance, but I've become a lot of emails describing everything I had to doo in detail, which was very nice! I didn't feel like I needed more assistance. 
We had one introduction lesson with a PowerPoint presentation for Erasmus students. That was very nice.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found it through the website HousingAnywhere. Later I figured that the website WG-gesucht would have been a better chose.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Rather spend some time searching for a nice place and a nice "WG" (Wohngemeinschaft), because you are going to spend a lot of time with your roomies. Don't just choose the easiest option.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I read that all the student housings were very far away from Campus and additionally you're not secured a room there, so if you a apply, maybe you have to find your own housing anyway. That's why I chose to find my own.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I only had clinical rotations. It was very nice of the Erasmus coordinator, that she organized the first clinical rotation for me. It was kind of stressfull to organize the other ones, because several departments never answered my emails.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: First you apply for an Erasmus exchange, next you apply to enroll at the University and you have to do an online german test. Next you have to send a lot of documents to actually enroll to the university and pay the semester fees. Then you can beginn to send emails to the departments in which you want to do your clinical rotations - some of them aqcuire a lot of documents too. When you've organized that, you have to send your plan to the coordinator. Lastly you have to get a couple of vaccines and blood samples and a signature from your general practitioner in Denmark.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The coordinator, Nikola Lepom, has been a great help throughout the process. She also helped organize the first clinical rotation.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: The departments which I firsted emailed never answered, so I didn't get my first priority, but I figured it all out in the end. I'm just happy I managed to get clinical rotations at departments, that will be accepted in Denmark.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Start early, so it isn't stressful. It always takes longer time than you expect, because you have to wait for so many different people to respond to your emails.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Only clinical rotations.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The hospitals are kind of different. At Charité it's way less digitalised in it is in the hospitals near Copenhagen. Also it's the doctors job to draw blood in Germany, while it's something the nurses do in Denmark, which is why I've gotten really good at drawing blood and at doing similar procedures.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Clinical rotations:
- Department of Infectious Diseases at CVK
- Department of musculoskeletal surgery at CCM

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I can indeed recommend the Department of Infectious Diseases at CVK, but I didn't really like the Department of musculoskeletal surgery at CCM.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Semester fees (the public transportation/a Deutschlandsemesterticket was included). It was 300 euros 3 months before my arrival, which I didn't expect.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Doing sports and taking classes offered to students! They are very cheap and very good. I can indeed recommend. It's also a nice way to get to know other students at the university.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I took dance-classes, arabic classes and a presemester iintesive german course. All of it was very nice and I can indeed recommend it to others. The only less nice thing is, that the courses start in the beginning of the german semester (mid or end October), which was half way through my exchange (because I had to end my exchange in the middle of December), so I couldn't stay until the end of the courses.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Everything you can imagine!! Humboldt University is huge and they have maybe 200 or more different activities to choose from. They have everything you can think of! You just have to be quick, because the spots are quickly sold out.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I did latin dance and arabic - both were very nice. I also did a presemester intensive german course, which means I got to know a lot of international students and other Erasmus students even before the semester started. I'm not that much into clubbing, but if you're you will have 50-100 Erasmus students who will happily accompany you to the clubs and party with you.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Stay in Berlin and spend time with the people you're getting to know! The time is so short, so the faster you're getting friends the more you're going to enjoy. Also visit Christmas markets, when that time of the year comes.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. Everyone is very open minded and welcoming. And also I don't feel the differences between and Denmark and Germany are huge. I keep forgetting to give tips in restaurants though, because I'm not used to it. Other than that the language has been the biggest challenge - writing admission letters in german was indeed a challenge.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer:
Do sports and activities offered by the University - that's the easiest way to get in touch with germans. Or find a "WG" with german students - I wish I would have done that. 
Other than that attend to Erasmus activities - a lot of german students are there too!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
Giving tips at restaurants.
The language. 
And I also lived the two from Parkistan, who didn't know how to sort waste, which was also kind of challenging haha.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: That everyone is so open and welcoming, and that so many german students are organizing those Erasmus events.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Do the "Farma"-exam in the 7th semester and attend a presemester german course before the exchange. It was very nice and a very nice way to extend the very short exchange. 
Sign up for sport classes or whatever you want - as long as you're meeting new people!
Attend to the Erasmix-events. They are very nice.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: It might be more difficult to get all the signatures you need from UCPH than it would have been in Denmark. The last year medical students in Germany are doing less than what UCPH expect Danish students to in their fourth year, which makes it difficult.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Speaking to patients in German and building a connection with them in a language that's not your mothertongue. I went to Germany half a year in my gap year, which means German is NOT my mothertonuge, and that's why it feels very good everything I've succeed with something here (speaking with patients, understanding lectures or writing admission letters).

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The language and learning all the medical terms in German, but that was indeed also one of the best parts of the exchange! And it feels very rewarding afterwards.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Actually I think I would recommend to do the exchange in the 11th semester instead of the 8th as I did. At that time you're more flexible, you can choose whatever departments you want and you don't have an OSCE exam waiting for you when you get home.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
